newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Feb 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Feb 7.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Friday:

* President Clinton unveiled a $1.69 trillion budget for 1998 that he said cuts taxes on the middle class, raises education and health care spending and shrinks the deficit until it becomes a $17 billion surplus in 2002.

* Deals that await negotiation with any debate over Clinton's budget include a way to cut capital gains taxes and a way to change the calculation of inflation, which would slow cost-of-living increases in Social Security payments and those of other federal programmes.
* A federal grand jury subpoenaed 10 years of financial records from New York City's 29,000-member police union as part of a widening investigation into allegations of corruption.

* One or two F-16 jet fighters repeatedly closed in on a passenger jet bound for Kennedy International Airport Wednesday afternoon, forcing the airliner to land. Military officials gave conflicting explanations about why the fighters got so close to the passenger jet.
* Thousands of students could get extra points on their college admissions exams because an 18-year-old New Hampshire student has found an error on the test administered last October.
* North Korea has agreed to accept up to 200,000 barrels of nuclear waste, adding new hostility to the tensions between North and South Korea.
